claims.statement: The PostgreSQL + pgvector schema is owned by hand-written Alembic migrations under `backend/alembic/versions/`. SQLAlchemy 2.x models in `backend/app/models/` mirror the schema and never generate migrations; the release gate (`make release-check`) fails if Alembic reports more than one head. The deploy script widens the alembic version column and runs `alembic upgrade head` against the new image BEFORE bringing up the inactive web color.

Knowledge chunks live in `KnowledgeBase` and `KnowledgeChunk` models with the embedding column declared via `pgvector`. `backend/app/core/vector.py` exposes `vec_literal` for SQLAlchemy queries; the retrieval layer ranks by cosine similarity + lexical overlap and re-ranks in the graph layer (`backend/app/graph/grounding.py`). `embedding_dim` is sourced from `Settings.openrouter_embedding_dim` (default from `OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL`) and validated on every insert.

Multi-head migrations are forbidden: `alembic heads | wc -l == 1` is a binary release gate. `scripts.widen_alembic_version` runs before `alembic upgrade head` to keep the alembic version column wide enough for future migrations. The partial unique index `uq_channel_accounts_one_active_facebook_messenger` enforces single-active Facebook Page at the DB level.

`make db` brings up Postgres + pgvector + Redis + Adminer in docker, runs the alembic baseline, and creates a default admin (`admin@vfic.dev` / `admin123`) via `backend/scripts/create_admin.py`. `make restore` overwrites the local DB from a backup, stamps alembic at head, and resets every user's password to `admin123` so a fresh checkout can run the full app without re-onboarding.
